asks_for: Describe the AEM Sites delivery approach and the university decisions needed to establish scope and schedule.
Explain how approved Drupal content and Spanish equivalents would be assessed, migrated and reconciled.
Describe the creation and accessibility assessment of reusable page layouts and editor-created content.
Explain editorial workflows, publishing controls and faculty access arrangements in AEM Sites.
Propose how retained downloadable documents would be cleaned up, made accessible, owned and linked without a new asset-management license.
Describe URL, redirect, metadata and journey checks that would protect search visibility and inbound links during migration.
Explain delivery of twelve accessible AEM Forms journeys with validation, confirmations and appropriate requested fields.
Describe reliable form submission integration with Dynamics 365 including duplicates, failures and investigation.
Propose applicant access to application paperwork and staff administration through Entra ID with clear identity dependencies.
Describe implementation of three Acrobat Sign processes and the university decisions required before use.
Explain how authorised CRM and Genesys Cloud CX staff would receive and interpret form and signature status.
Describe a reconciled and privacy-conscious reporting feed to Snowflake for Power BI.
Explain setup and governance of up to four concurrent Target experiments on public recruitment pages.
Propose measurement and consent behaviour for privacy review and verification across the three recruitment markets.
Describe performance and availability targets and verification with Cloudflare and peak traffic taken into account.
Explain integrated testing, safe test data, recovery checks and defect reporting for the launch decision.
Describe role-based training, handover and cutover preparation for the pilot and main launch.
Set out the first six months of support including incidents, changes, release checks, reporting and university responsibilities.
Explain hosting, data locations, component operators and unresolved licensing or contractual dependencies.
Describe privileged access and credential controls for delivery staff, support staff and subcontractors.
Explain retention, deletion, access requests and audit records with policy dependencies and practical limitations.
Describe security incident, vulnerability and recovery arrangements including university and provider participation.
Provide two relevant engagement examples with the supplier's responsibilities, scale and outcomes.
Explain available reference evidence, permission arrangements and gaps in directly comparable experience.
Propose delivery and support staffing with allocations, locations, subcontractors and continuity arrangements.
Describe estimation, governance, acceptance, change control and escalation of schedule risks.
